items.title: Charles L. Dufour Interview, 1958-05-14
items.q: This is Mr. Hilliard, my brother-in-law, Mr. LeBuff

ctx.x: jazz and ragtime. Did they tend to play pat music? They played what was hot for the day. Jada, Jada, Jing, Jing, Jing. Purdy Baby. That sort of stuff. But where, 20 years earlier, they were playing, I Wonder Who's Kissing Her Now, which would be Walsey. The thing was pepped up and jazzed up, as the expression went. The music was definitely jazzed up. I would say that that was part of the evolution, yes. Did you tend to hire a lot of the... Once again, I can't answer. Didn't tend to have a lot of colored bands. I…

knowing, I would say that there was no... That there were considerably considerable color bands used. What about it? Buckle such as Debuiton parties, where they have a gas band at a Debutant party? I can't answer that question. Like I say, I wasn't a DD. All right. Well, you said that. Here comes somebody who might be able to answer your question, Mark. Polly? Yeah. This is Mr. Hilliard, my brother-in-law, Mr. LeBuff, Mr. Never coming in and getting away from

me. He said, they do more far off. Didn't you look a little bit like before? More than I did. Well, you said that the gaze didn't offend you. You know, did a lot of people say that they were just rotten, gutter-clapted, claps? A lot of people did. And I wouldn't doubt for a moment that I went through a period in which I felt that.
